verses.author: model_A
verses.text: She folds the letter twice before deciding not to send it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles on the windowsill
where she once wrote his name—
now just a smudge of light.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle forgets to whistle—
steam fogs the mirror
where no one is looking back.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A dog barks twice at the gate—
someone's shadow
crossing where the fence used to end.

Someone left the porch light burning—

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mailbox leans a little more each spring—
weeds climb the post
where nobody checks for letters.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The gutter drips a slow count—
rust blooms on the roof
where someone once patched the leak.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's cat sleeps in the empty planter—
soil gone dry
where nothing's grown in years.
